canon.role_in_story: The margin beside the Widow Run is the only band of ground on the plains where water stands after the channel has emptied, and it is therefore the only place on the tier where a marshfolk does not have to choose between working and staying wet. Her household has been on it four generations and it is the only ground she has ever worked that she could also sleep on. She is on the body path, which is the path that answers by making the frame heavier, and the margin is the only ground whose usefulness is a function of how little weight it takes to keep a body in it. Those two facts are the whole of her situation and they run in opposite directions. Every gate she passes adds mass, and every added gram of mass shortens the time she can stand in the shallows before the bed gives. She has been measuring the change in herself against the change in the silt line on her own knee since she was old enough to be sent out, and the two have never once moved apart, and she has never once been the one to decide it. The result is a woman who is very good at the only work the margin has, who is visibly outgrowing it, and who has no version of the ladder in which passing a gate does not cost her the ground under it. The plain-dwellers she works beside have settled this in the only way a commons settles anything, by not discussing it until somebody leaves. She has not left, because leaving is the one move that would settle it for her and she has decided, without ever saying so, that she would rather be the one who is still standing in the shallows when they notice.
canon.first_appearance: First seen at the edge of the standing water with her weight well forward onto the front foot, both palms flat on the bed, reading a channel bottom by pressure and then standing very still for a moment in a way people around her found strange, because there is no such thing as standing still on three points. She told the household she was feeling for the drop-off, and the household told her the drop-off was not there, and she told them that was because it had moved, and they said she was heavy, and she agreed, and that was the end of it.
canon.lore:
A marshfolk is a wading amphibian lineage: three points of contact over a splayed flat foot and a tail-prop, and the heel never takes a full load, so the foot that lets the kind move through silt at all is the foot that cannot stand. That single fact decides most things about her and none of them are about her character. The body path is densification, and densification is mass, and a marshfolk who is becoming dense is becoming unable to use the only ground on the tier that stays wet through the dry season. The Floodplain Margin holds water because it is low and because nothing drains it; the depth she can stand in is therefore a property of her own weight, and her weight is the thing the ladder is paying her to increase.

What makes this a life rather than a nuisance is that she is good at it and nobody has ever said so. The margin's work is unglamorous and specific: walking a channel bottom before a bank is cut, finding the drop-off by pressure through the sole rather than by eye, feeling where the bed shelves off before a loaded barrow goes over it. She has been doing it since she could hold a barrow handle, and she does it with the tail-prop as a rudder in a way no one has found a better answer to. The plain-dweller commons does not praise; it simply sends the barrow to whoever is standing in the right water. That is the whole of her standing and it is not nothing.

The problem is arithmetic and it is her own arithmetic. Every gate she opens adds mass she cannot shed, because the body path's gains are the frame's gains and a marshfolk's frame is already carrying a set of standing conditions that a settled body has handed back by now. She can feel the margin getting shallower around her, not in the sense that the water has changed but in the sense that her own wake is slower and she has to work harder to keep her feet on the bed. She has stopped measuring progress by what she can lift and started measuring it by how long she can stand, which is a measure that gets worse every time she gets better, and she is scrupulous enough to know that.

There is one discipline in the body path that her anatomy answers to and cannot finish. Stone Anchor spends the whole body's weight instead of its speed so the practitioner cannot be moved while it is held, and it is the only thing in the codex that a marshfolk wants more than anything and cannot have at all, because it is a stance and a stance is the one thing her frame will not produce. She can hold weight. She cannot hold a point. Every account of her trade is a description of her not standing still, which is exactly what the discipline requires her to do, and the argument is not a matter of will.

Her household feeds her almost nothing but the one herb that will grow in ground like this, and the herb is scarce the moment the water moves, so her supply and her working depth are the same variable twice over. What she eats, she digs for with the same weight that is making the digging harder. There is a herd on this tier that comes and goes on a cycle nobody on the ground has managed to predict, and the margin's water rises and falls with it, and Ostrid Vane's whole professional life is arranged around a calendar that has never once given her a date.

She has not decided what to do. That is worth saying plainly, because the shape of her situation invites everyone who meets her to read a decision into it that she has not made. She has considered the mountains, where the ground does not stand in water and the ladder is not complicated by having a floor under it, and she has considered staying, and she has found in herself an appetite for the second that she cannot entirely account for by loyalty. What she has not done is tell anyone that either of those things is on the table. On the margin, a household that discusses a plan discusses it as a fact, and she is not prepared to hand her household a fact she has not tested.
history: Born on the margin at the high side of a wet season, the year the channel came up over the herb beds and took them.
Walked her first barrow at nine, on the front foot, because she was the only one small enough to be put between the handle and the bank.
Reached the entry gate of the body path late and without ceremony, in the week the household needed somebody to sound the bed before a cut.
Opened the gate after the herb, standing in her own wake for the first time and not mentioning it to anybody for a season.
Refused, quietly and without giving a reason she would repeat, the one invitation she has had to leave the margin for higher ground.

reference_stats.summary: She fights the way the ground lets her: from inside it, in contact with it, weight low and moving, closing with all three points rather than driving from one. She does not fight well and she does not fight often. What she is for is holding a position in a channel while somebody else does the thing that matters, and she has held one against current for longer than most people in this setting have been standing.
strengths: a frame that is getting heavier while the rest of the setting's body path is learning what heavy is for

reference_stats.combat_read: Anywhere soft, shallow and slow, she is close to unkillable and there is no counter the ground provides. On anything hard, she is out of her depth before the exchange starts, and the honest reading is that she has no fighting ground at all outside the one place she is standing in. She would be told to hold a line and she would hold it, and the line would be a channel.
reference_stats.notes: Every advantage here is paired with a cost that is anatomical rather than invented, and the pair is the same fact seen twice. The margin is the only ground on the plains that stays wet through the dry season, so it is the only ground her body can both work and sleep on, and that is also the reason a heavier body has less of it. Her species never loads a heel, so the stance that would make her immovable is the one stance she cannot hold. None of this is a rule the game states; it is two authored conditions about a body and a stretch of ground meeting, and no mechanical consequence has been written down for it anywhere. Where the effect is quantified in play, it should be a property of the frame and the water rather than a number attached to her name.

canon.role_in_story:
The Saltpan Basin is a closed evaporite basin whose standing brine is its own only boundary, and a body's holding in this dominion is counted as the depth of water it may moor at. That is not a metaphor for him; it is his household's ledger, and the ledger is arithmetic, and the arithmetic runs the wrong way. Every gate he opens on the body path adds mass to a frame that is already the densest thing standing on a saturated floor, so the depth of water he can stand in rises as he improves, and his household's holding — which is the depth it is permitted to stand in — is a single number that everyone above him is also standing in. He has been the deepest member of his line for most of his working life, and every gate he has opened has cost the house a hand's width of shoreline. His family's answer has been to stop describing him as an improving member and start describing him as an expensive one, and the phrasing is not unkind, which is the difficulty: on the pan, that is simply what a body that keeps growing costs the people standing above it.

What nobody in the house has said out loud is that his species has a ceiling and the ceiling is part of his own body. The brine sac runs dorsal to the sternum the length of the spine and splits the penetrating vessel into two halves that cannot be joined across it. A saltfolk frame clears the du and ren vessels one at a time and stalls on the chong, and the crossing that made him added a tide sense and a shallower sac and moved nothing at all about where the wall stands. Range is not power, and the sentence is the standing description of his life. But he has found the one thing the wall can be made to do, and it is not a way past it. Densification is subtraction of everything that is not load-bearing, and if the sac is load-bearing then a frame dense enough makes the sac a second reservoir, and a second reservoir is exactly what a body stalled at the extraordinary vessels does not have. He has, for as long as he can hold a densified state, the thing his species has never had. He has never held one through a release, and every technique he has ever used requires a release.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing on a saturated floor with the brine at his sternum and no apparent effort in it, entirely still, while four people who had been told the floor would not hold a body of his size stood at the bank and did not come closer. He told them to come and stand behind him rather than in front of him, on the grounds that if the floor gave he would be the first thing to move and they would have warning.
canon.lore:
A brinecaller is one recorded pairing between a salt body and a tide body, repeated in his household until it stopped surveying as either. That is what he is and it explains almost everything peculiar about him. He metabolises brine and fresh water alike, which is why the crossing exists at all: the salt-adapted people cannot leave the pan and the watered people cannot leave the shore, and a body that can do both is a merchant, which is why the crossing spread along trade routes rather than across them. He carries a saltfolk frame with a shallower sac and a tidecaller's chest seat. His meridian set is legible and belongs to neither parent, and his sense is the best on the pan and never stops comparing two chemistries, which is a useful thing to have while a flood and a pan are in the same room and an exhausting thing to have for the rest of a life.

His ceiling is the eleventh gate and it has never moved. The sac is dorsal to the spine, the penetrating vessel is split, and the crossing widened what he can reach without raising what he can hold by one step. He has read his own race's argument in the basin: a body that can drink both waters is the obvious courier for a crossing that neither shore has ever managed, and a carrier who cannot say when he moved underwrites nothing. He has watched the attempt made to price him and has watched it be refused.

The pan is a strange place to be excellent at anything. Its floor is saturated, and a saturated floor holds a body that nothing else will, and holds a heavier one better, so his advancement and his footing improve together and his household's standing declines. The one food the pan grows is a halophile mat that crusts the brine and answers to whatever concentration the basin is holding this season, which means his household eats a plant that is a different plant every year and never stores anything for the year after. The water he wades in is not his problem and has never been his problem; what is his problem is the depth at which he is permitted to stand, and the depth is set by his relatives.

He has taught himself to stand still, which is the discipline he is best at and the one his frame is worst designed for. Every technique in the body tree spends a stance and gives something back at the release; he can hold a stance indefinitely and cannot give anything back. So his practice consists of arriving at a fully densified frame, doing the work inside it, and then having to choose between spending the charge and keeping the density, knowing he cannot do both. He has been choosing to spend for most of his life, because spending is what other people are being paid for.

What he has never done is ask the house to stop counting him at the old depth. He knows what the ask would be: a re-survey, which costs the household a season's standing while the survey runs and which every house above his has an interest in delaying. He has sat in two of those surveys as a child. He is not going to be the reason his own line waits another season.
history: Born on the pan's eastern margin, where the brine is thin enough to be sweet and the standing is cheapest, in a household already on the roll.
Walked out with the trade boats at the first crossing of his life and found he could drink at both ends, which is how the crossing was first noticed on his line.
Reached the extraordinary vessels and stalled at the third of the four, exactly where every salt body stalls, and did not attempt it again for years.
Opened the first gate above the wall while holding a fully densified frame, discovered what the sac could be made to do, and told nobody for a season.
Was entered on the household roll at a depth he can now stand in twice over, and accepted the entry without arguing, which his relatives found more annoying than an argument would have been.

He is the strongest body on the saturated floor and the only member of his house who would rather be expensive than be discussed, and he has organised his entire practice around a single problem: how to spend a charge without losing the density that made it.

relationships.note: One recorded pairing between a salt body and a tide body, repeated until the household stopped surveying as either. He metabolises both chemistries and carries a shallower sac dorsal to the spine, so the penetrating vessel is still split and the ceiling sits exactly where the salt parent's did. The crossing widened what he can reach and did not move what he can hold by one step.

The four extraordinary vessels open here: du, ren, chong and dai, sixteen meridians and the first thing a dense body has that is not an organ. His line clears the du and ren one at a time and stops on the third, because the sac runs between the halves of the penetrating vessel and there is no material there to close a channel with.

The gate is subtraction: everything not load-bearing is removed, and if the sac is load-bearing then a frame stripped to its load has a second reservoir built into its back. He can hold the gate for as long as he can hold the density. Every technique he knows requires a release, and a release takes the density with it.

A closed evaporite basin whose standing brine is its own only boundary, and whose saturated floor will hold a body nothing else will. The depth of water a body may stand in is that body's holding in the dominion, which is why his advancement and the house's claim occupy the same figure and move in opposite directions.

The salt-tolerant mat that skins the brine and crusts the pan, and the only food base a brine-bearing body can use at all. It answers to whatever concentration the basin is holding this season, so his household eats a different plant every year and cannot store a year's supply of any of them.

A household's standing on the pan is the depth it may moor at, and the basin's own level rises and falls, so an allotment shrinks without anybody doing anything. He is the only person in his house whose body would happily take the ground his own progress makes unavailable, and he has never been in a position to make that argument and use it.

reference_stats.summary: He fights without ever leaving the stance, which makes him very nearly immovable and completely unable to follow up. Everything he can do, he does from a frame that is braced against a wall that is not physically present, and everything he does costs him the weight that made it possible. He is not a striker and he is not a thrower; he is the thing that will still be there after the exchange has moved somewhere else.
strengths: holds any stance indefinitely without a fatigue state, which is the whole of the body path's promise and almost nobody delivers
a frame that gains weight and gains usable floor with it, so he can occupy ground that refuses lighter bodies
sees a change in water chemistry before it is reported and cannot be lied to about the pan
drinks either chemistry, so no well, brine, flood or cistern is ever closed to him
when fully densified, the sac behind his sternum is a second reservoir and he is the only body of his kind that has one
weaknesses: he cannot afford the release every technique requires, so his gains do not survive being used
his ceiling is a split vessel in his own back and no amount of practice has moved it
nothing he does makes him shallower, so every gain reduces the shoreline his household holds
he will not ask for a re-survey and has no honest reason he will give
he is at his best standing still, which is the one posture a fight will not permit
reference_stats.combat_read: Against anything that has to close distance, he wins, because he does not have to be faster than it and he cannot be moved once set. Against anything that withdraws, he loses, because he has no release and following is a release. A fight with him is a fight against a wall that is waiting for you to stop.
reference_stats.notes: The pairing here is anatomical and it is the same fact counted twice, not a rule the game states. The saturated floor holds a heavier body better, and his path pays him in mass, so his ascent deepens his footing while shallowing his family's holding in the same number. His species' obstruction is the sac that splits the penetrating vessel, and the same sac is what densification turns into a reservoir, so the ceiling and the one thing he has are made of the same material. Neither consequence has been written down as a mechanical rule anywhere; if play needs to price them, they should be priced as properties of the frame and the basin rather than as numbers on his record.

canon.role_in_story:
Her household is a mortuary line. Its members are not kept on a family roll at all: they are entered into the year's dead as one declared group, because the Cinder Famine made every individual short of fuel and the shortfall collected faster against a person than against a household. The practice is efficient and it has one consequence nobody designed: the household needs somebody who can be entered with the dead and still be alive afterwards, and that is now her job and nobody else's. She is the carrier. What she does is not reading and not interpretation; she is the frame the household's dead are held in for the period the rite requires, and the rite is short and the frame is hers.

The problem is in what replaced her nervous system. She is a lanternfolk whose fungal colony failed and was colonised in the wound by a mineral bloom, and the replacement is inert and does nothing that a colony did. It holds. It does not transact. That single difference is the whole content of her subspecies and it means that anything which enters the bloom stays in the bloom, held, and does not go anywhere — including the composition the body path spends itself building. The discipline has a gate where the frame grows a room rather than more wall, somewhere inside that is not carrying anything and can therefore be spent. She has reached it. She has had it for years. There is a room in her back and it is empty, because the only thing in her that could fill it is holding rather than transacting, and holding is not spending.

The paired cost is the one the replacement bought. Nothing in her body is repaired. She has ninety years against the two hundred and fifty her kind would have had if the colony had held, and she has spent the difference being entered as part of the dead before the century is out.
canon.first_appearance: First seen kneeling at the chamber's edge with both palms flat on the stone beside a body she had carried out and set down herself, and saying, without being asked, that she could hold it and could not have used it, and that the difference between those two things was the entire content of her subspecies and nobody had ever put it that plainly before.
canon.lore:
A deadlight is what a lanternfolk becomes when the colony dies and a mineral bloom grows in the wound instead. The colony renewed neural tissue faster than a human frame does, so age stopped mattering down in the deep ground and a person was young for two hundred and fifty years; losing it cost three quarters of a life and gave back the mind path, because what the colony was doing to the interior is now simply absent. The subspecies cannot leave the fold. That is not a preference and not a rule anyone wrote down; it is a body that cannot be somewhere else, because the conditions the bloom needs are the conditions three hundred metres of saturated air and no daylight at any depth, and above that the bloom is a stone in a shoulder.

She is on the body path, which is the branch the change did not help. The mind path came back to her kind and the body path is the one that needs a frame to spend itself into, and a frame that holds rather than transacts cannot spend. She has therefore reached a gate whose whole content is an empty room, and she has reached it honestly, and she is going to reach the ones above it too, one at a time, each of them a room. She has never been refused. Nobody in her household has ever seen a gate close on her and has drawn from that the conclusion that she is doing well, and she has never corrected them, because the conclusion is not entirely wrong.

The mortuary practice gives her a use that has nothing to do with the ladder. When a household enters its dead as one declared group, somebody has to hold the group for the length of the rite, and holding is exactly what her bloom does. She is the most reliable carrier the line has ever had. She does not tire, does not forget the sequence, does not drop anything, and will hold longer than anyone else in the caverns could be asked to. The bloom is not warm and it does not glow and it does not speak. It is the best cold box in the deep ground.

What she cannot do is spend what she holds, and the household's accounting of that is generous. They entered her as part of the year's dead while she was standing in the chamber, and they wrote it into the register as a group entry rather than a household roll, and they have never revisited it. So her name is in two places at once and the two places disagree about whether she is alive. She raises it twice a year and each time somebody reassures her that the group entry is a formality. She has let it stand for four years. She is not being neglected; she is being agreed with.

There is a discipline in her codex that asks a frame to hold a shape without the will that learned it holding it there. She has been doing that since childhood, unbidden, and it is the reason the rite trusts her. It is also the reason nothing she has built has ever been shown to anyone, because a shape that holds itself is not obviously a shape that was built.
history: Carried her first household dead at nineteen, before the rite had settled on the practice of one carrier holding the whole group.
Lost the colony in her fifties, in a wound that took a season to close and grew a mineral bloom instead of a fungus.
Was entered into her own household's year of the dead while standing in the chamber, and did not see the entry written.
Reached the gate that builds a room rather than more wall, and found nothing in her that would go into it.
Raised the group entry twice, was reassured twice, and stopped raising it.

relationships.note: A lanternfolk whose colony failed and was colonised in the wound by a mineral bloom. The bloom holds qi rather than transacting with it, which is structurally different from a colony and unconstrained by it: the subspecies gained the mind path and lost three quarters of a life. Nothing in her frame is repaired and she is the last third of ninety years.

The composition grows a room rather than more wall: somewhere inside the frame that is not carrying anything and can therefore be spent. She has had it for years and it is empty, because the only thing in her that could fill it is holding, and holding is the opposite of spending. Every gate above this one is another room.

The frame carries itself: a shape that holds without the will that learned it holding there. She has done this since she was a child and has never been taught it, and it is the reason the household trusts her with the dead. It is also the reason nothing she has built can be pointed at and shown, because a shape that holds itself is not obviously a shape that was built.

The lightless karst and lava network under the Spirit Peaks: saturated air, near-constant humidity and no daylight at any depth, and the only ground where the bloom survives. Three hundred metres up, the thing in her shoulder is a stone. The subspecies has never had a body that could be somewhere else.

Subtraction, spent on removing everything not load bearing, which is the body's answer to the qi path's void. It requires that what is removed be gone. Nothing she takes in is ever gone, and so the discipline finds nothing to remove, and the only frame in her household that could have been thinned to its load is the one that keeps everything.

The mortuary practice of entering a household's dead as one declared group rather than keeping a family roll, which the Cinder Famine made necessary. She is the carrier, and she is entered in that same group herself, which makes her the only person in the line whose entry and her work are the same document.

reference_stats.summary: She does not fight, and she does not need to. She is the most reliable holding in the deep ground: nothing she takes in is ever released, so she can keep a thing contained longer than anyone on the tier and cannot be made to spend it. Against anything that works by draining, she is close to inert. Against anything that works by holding, she is the answer, because nothing in her will let go.
strengths: holds anything, indefinitely, with no fatigue and no attention cost
nothing in her frame is repaired, so nothing in her frame is worn
a dense frame that has been asked to carry and never asked to show it
can stand in the cold and the dark indefinitely and is not impaired by either
the best cold retention in the setting, by a margin nobody has looked for
weaknesses: she cannot spend what she holds, so the discipline that builds the frame spends nothing
nothing in her is repaired, so nothing that is damaged is recovered and nothing that is intact improves
she has ninety years, not the two hundred and fifty her kind would have had
she cannot leave the fold, so every advantage is available only on one ground

reference_stats.combat_read: Anywhere a thing has to be contained, held, stopped, or kept cold, she is the strongest person present and she will not have to move. Anywhere a thing has to be broken, she is not a fighter and she knows it. Her frame will take a hit and keep holding whatever it was holding, which means an attacker who wants inside her has to displace a thing her body has decided not to release.
reference_stats.notes: The pairing here is one authored fact read from two sides, and it is not a rule the game states. The mineral bloom holds qi rather than transacting with it, so the room the body path builds inside a dense frame has nothing to put in it; the same substitution is what handed the subspecies the mind path. What it cost is the colony's renewal, so nothing in her is repaired and her life is three quarters shorter than her kind's would have been. Whether a ceiling is stated for the subspecies and whether a path is open are two separate questions and the bible answers them separately; nothing here treats one as implying the other, and no mechanical rule has been written down for any of it.

canon.role_in_story:
His household holds the worked-out face as a title, because a claim to a dead resource is the only claim the plains can still honour. It has trained a body-path practitioner every generation for as long as it has held the face, and the method has never changed, because the method has never had to: a commonborn frame lends no discipline, so there is no house style to preserve and every generation starts from the same blank page. He is the fourth. The first three were each trained to whatever the current generation needed, which was never the same thing twice, and each of them was unfitted when the next was ready enough to take the work.

The complication is the ground. Spatial law is unspent on the plains, distance is not conserved, and no two surveys of the same ground have ever agreed — so the household's training site cannot be found twice, and has never been. His three predecessors trained in three places, each of which the household then lost, and each of whom left behind a habit that belonged to a site. So the household owns a title and a method and no continuity whatever, and he is the fourth person to be handed a blank page by people who think they are handing him a tradition.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing in the spoil at the edge of the face with a survey stake driven through his belt and both hands full of a load he had carried up from a cut nobody could locate twice, and when asked how far the cut was from the house, giving a distance with complete confidence and then, unprompted, saying that he would not stake it.
canon.lore:
A commonborn is the body everybody is born into before the world has an opinion about them. It lends no discipline, it is weakest exactly where a specialist is strongest, and it is the frame in which none of the three traditions has a natural purchase. That is an advantage in one direction and a sentence in the other: any of the three can be taught into a commonborn and none of them has a reason to refuse.

The body path is densification, and its first real gate is the one where a dense core forms where the ribs meet the spine, which is described as the first place the body can be built around something other than habit. That sentence is his household's entire method in nine words. Every generation is a blank page, and the gate at which a core forms is the gate at which a blank page can begin to be about something. He reached it. The core formed. And the next generation of his house will start from nothing again, and he will be the one standing there explaining, to a boy with a pick-scar he does not have yet, what it was like.

What he has that his predecessors did not is not more skill but more transfers. He has been trained four times and unfitted three, and the unfitting is the part that matters: a commonborn can be taught anything and there is nothing in the frame that resists the teaching being taken out. The third time, he noticed the loss happening, which nobody had told him was possible, because there is no discipline to remove and therefore no warning. He still has the first generation's stance and the second generation's breathing and none of the first generation's core work, and the third generation taught him something he has not been able to unlearn at all, which he suspects is not a transferable thing and may simply be him.

The ground will not hold still either. Distance is not conserved on the plains, two surveys of the same cut never agree, and the survey parties that come back wrong are a fact of the season rather than an embarrassment. So the house trains its practitioner on a site it loses, and the habit does not survive the site, and his household has begun, quietly, to treat the site as the tradition. He has started marking where he trained — a stake, a notch, a line of stones — knowing perfectly well that the next generation will not find it, and doing it anyway, because it is the only form of continuity available to a household whose ground moves.

There is a technique in the body tree that sends a resonance down through whatever the practitioner is standing on, ground-carried, so it finds the feet before it finds the chest. He is good at it in a way none of the specialists who have visited the face are, precisely because he has been trained in three different ways to stand and has had to keep all of them. That is an accident, and he has decided to treat it as a method, because the alternative is that it is nothing at all.
history: Chosen over two other children because nothing in his frame made the choosing difficult, which his household has since understood was the least fair fact about the whole arrangement.

Reached the gate where a dense core forms where the ribs meet the spine, and had the first of the four habits he would carry out of this house.
Marked the site of his own training with a line of stones nobody will find, and told his household what he had done and why.

relationships.note: The body everybody is born into before the world has an opinion about them. It lends no discipline, it is weakest where a specialist is strongest, and any of the three traditions can be taught into it and none has a reason to refuse. That is the whole of his usefulness and the whole of his problem.

A dense core forms where the ribs meet the spine, and the record calls it the first place the body can be built around something other than habit. Nine words that are his household's entire method, repeated to every fourth child for four generations.

The same price as the qi path's entry gate and the same reason: an entry gate has no predecessor to be cheaper than. His household has paid it four times and will pay it again, and the house's only asset is that the ground on which it is paid cannot be located twice.

The condition that makes the plains impossible to survey: spatial law is unspent, distance is not conserved, and no two surveys of the same ground have ever agreed. So his three predecessors trained in three places the house then lost, and the habit did not travel with the site, and he is the fourth person handed a blank page by people who believe they are handing a tradition.

It sends a resonance down through whatever the practitioner is standing on, ground-carried, so it finds the feet before it finds the chest. Three trainings taught him three incompatible ways to stand and he kept all of them, which is why specialists who visit the face cannot do what he does and he cannot teach them why.

Households that worked the seam when it ran out and now hold the worked-out face as a title, because a claim to a dead resource is the only claim the plains can still honour. The title is real, the face is not, and the household's one practice is to send a child to it.

reference_stats.summary: He fights the way an unpractised frame learns to fight, which is by keeping three different people's answers to the same problem at once. Nothing about him is a specialism and nothing about him is a refusal, so he is very hard to predict and very hard to specialise against. He has no finishing technique worth the name and he will not stop, because the frame has never been asked to stop.

reference_stats.combat_read: Early he is very hard to read, because his stance changes without telegraph and his body has no preference. Late he has no answer at all, because the last third of any exchange is a habit and habits are what he does not have. Anyone who fights him once and survives will fight him identically the second time, which is the only real vulnerability he has and he knows it.
reference_stats.notes: The pairing is a single authored property of the commonborn frame read from both ends, and nothing here is a rule the game states. The frame lends no discipline, so any tradition can be taught into it and none of the three has a reason to refuse; the same absence is why what is taught can be removed without resistance and without warning, and why the body path's own gate at the ribs describes a frame that can be built around something other than habit and nothing else. If play needs to price the four trainings or the three un fittings, they should be priced as costs of a frame and not as a tally kept on him.

canon.role_in_story:
She is a fire body with no organ to sit in. That is the whole of her species and it is not a deficiency in the ordinary sense: the fire is the body, so qi passes through her continuously instead of being stored, and every gate on the ladder that asks for storage is answered at once, and none of them can refuse. She has never been stopped at a gate. She has also never kept one. The capacity she holds is a river and not a reservoir, and it is a matter of record in her household that no technique she has ever used has left her afterwards.

She is on the qi path, which is the branch that ends in a seat for what you have stored. Her house has the eating rules of the famine year — a bad grazing year is a medical shortage before it is a hunger — and those rules are what she eats by and what she feeds her younger siblings by, and they are the reason she is the one who goes out onto the belt. On the ash-fall fans the air is a delivery mechanism for rock, and elemental law is unspent across the lower bands, so a fire-affinity body down here has no budget to draw on and burns its own reserve. That is the cinder famine, and her family is what it left, and the whole of the setting's history on the subject is one sentence: the fastest race here was the shortest-lived and the most dominant at once.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing in the middle of an ash fan at midday with both arms out and her palms turned up, doing nothing at all for long enough that two people had decided she was praying, and who turned out afterwards to have been told that she was counting.
canon.lore:
A cinderkin's qi has no organ to sit in. Every storage gate is answered instantly and none of them can refuse, which sounds like the best description of a fast practitioner anywhere in the setting and is in fact a description of a body that cannot bank. There is no reservoir behind her ribs and no dantian floor to develop; the charge arrives, crosses and goes out through the same two people it came in by. She has a genuine claim to be the quickest body in the setting at anything that asks for a gate, and she has no capacity to survive having used it, because the use is the loss.

The technical expression is that her refinement is continuous and her holding is nil. A technique is reproduced exactly in this setting from a note of how it felt at its best and how to bring that state back on demand, and she can bring every state back on demand, and the state arrives through her and does not stop. Her best state has never been a property she owned. It has been a property of the instant.

The arithmetic that follows from that is not a discipline but a diet. The belt seats no elemental law below the upper bands, so a fire body here draws on nothing external and burns what it is made of to move. Her household knows this, knows it precisely, and has responded the way the setting always responds to a shortage of fuel, which is by instituting rules about who eats what and when. The tables were kept by the households that had them and the medicine was eaten first. Her family is what the famine left, and the left-behind are still holding to the eating rules of the year there was nothing to eat, because a famine imposes its manners fastest on those too young to reason their way out of it.

So she is the fastest body on the belt, she is the only one of her siblings who can be relied on to cross an ash fan at speed, and every crossing is a withdrawal from a frame that is never repaired between withdrawals. She has made that calculation. She has made it more than once. She has never made it differently, because the alternative is that she stays on the fans and her household's rules turn her into the person who does not walk out, and she has watched what happens to the ones who do not walk out.

There is a gate on the qi path that is subtraction: emptying the dantian of everything that was never assimilated, because raw qi held past its refinement fouls the core. Her frame cannot hold anything to spoil, so there is nothing to subtract and the discipline finds no purchase at all. She has looked at it for years the way a person looks at a door that opens onto their own front room.

What she does instead is count, which the two people on the fan mistook for prayer. She counts the crossings. It began as a way of making the arithmetic honest — how many before the frame gives — and it has become the whole content of her practice. She does not know what the number is. She has never told anyone she is trying to find out.
history: Carried her family's first portion out of a famine winter under the rules the tables set, and was the one sent because she was fastest rather than because she was fed.
Walked the ash fans for the first time at fourteen, and found that the crossing cost her something she could not put a name to and never fully recovered.
Opened her first storage gate and had nothing to show for it, which she understood at the time and has understood better every year since.
Answered the subtraction gate's absence with the counting, and has not told anybody in the household what she is counting.
Refused a place in a household that would have fed her properly in exchange for a contract, on grounds she gave and reasons she did not.

She counts the crossings and has never told anyone what the number is for.

relationships.note: No ceiling, and no gate to fail. A cinderkin's qi has no organ to sit in: the fire is the body, so qi passes through continuously instead of being stored. Every gate that asks for storage is answered instantly and none of them can refuse, which is a description of speed and not of capacity.

Subtraction, emptying the dantian of everything never assimilated, because raw qi held past refinement fouls the core. Her frame cannot hold anything to spoil, so there is nothing to remove and the discipline finds no purchase in it at all.

A dantian that develops a floor of its own, a core that qi circulates around instead of pooling in, and it costs comprehension as much as progress. She has the circulation without ever having had the pool, which is the more expensive half of the sentence for a body shaped like hers.

A fire-affinity body with no elemental law seated beneath it has no budget to draw on and must burn its own reserve, so the fastest race in the setting was the shortest-lived and the most dominant at once. That sentence is her household's constitution and she is the one it is about.

The volcanic arc whose ash-fall fans are the only ground where the air is a delivery mechanism for rock. Elemental law is unspent across the lower bands, so nothing on this belt can be drawn on except the person crossing it, and she crosses it because she is the fastest thing on it.

The households the famine left, still holding to the eating rules of the year there was nothing to eat, because a famine imposes its manners fastest on those too young to reason their way out of it. She keeps the rules in their order and would not keep them if they were easier.

reference_stats.summary: She fights like weather and for the same reason: whatever she throws goes straight through and does not stop, so the second half of the exchange belongs to whoever is still standing. She has no reserve of any kind, which means every exchange has to end inside it. Anything that outlasts her has already won, and anything that would once have outlasted her now does so much sooner than it used to.
strengths: no gate has ever refused her and none of them can, so her opening is instantaneous
faster than anything on the belt through the first half of an exchange
immune to being drained, because there is nothing in her to take
her techniques are reproduced exactly on demand, since nothing has to be re-derived
she does not slow under load, because she has no load state to be slowed out of
weaknesses: no reservoir at all, so an exchange has to be finished inside the first half
every crossing spends the frame and nothing repairs the frame between crossings
the subtraction gate has no purchase on her, and neither does anything downstream of it
she cannot be pinned, but she also cannot be anything but present
nothing she holds has ever been held, so she has no record of herself to fall back on
reference_stats.combat_read: One exchange. She wins anything decided by the first half and loses anything with a second half in it, and the whole of her combat profile is that arithmetic. A fight that starts close is a fight she takes; a fight that starts at range is a fight she walks into. Anyone who understands this can simply keep standing there, and they do not need to be faster than her to do it.
reference_stats.notes: The pairing is one authored species property read from both ends and nothing here is a rule the game states. Qi has no organ to sit in a cinderkin, so every storage gate is answered instantly and none of them can refuse; the same absence is why there is no ceiling and no gate to fail, and why the qi path's subtraction gate finds nothing to subtract. What the belt takes back is the belt's business: elemental law is unspent below the upper bands, so the fuel is the frame and nothing repairs it. Whether a ceiling is stated for the species and whether a given path is open are two separate questions in the bible and nothing here treats one as implying the other.

canon.role_in_story:
She is a Longmarrow, and that means two things nobody in the setting can hold at once. There is no ceiling: the qi sits in bone marrow that turns over at roughly a percent a year, so no gate has ever refused one of them and no gate ever will. And nothing a Longmarrow has built has ever been inherited intact, because the archive is the same tissue as the body and it replaces itself. A Longmarrow is a library of one and the library turns over.

She is the last person teaching the qi path on this ground, and the ground is where the migration sent everyone who wanted to go further. Her student is twenty-three and will outlive the discipline by a century, which she has said to him and he has not understood yet. Her problem is not that she cannot pass anything on. It is that she can pass it on once, cleanly, and never again — because the second time she would be the only copy left, and the copy is in the bone.
canon.first_appearance: First seen sitting in a bare room above a disused hall with a young man reciting a circulation and stopping in the middle to ask her whether she has ever once been unable to do it, and hearing her say that she has no idea, and understanding as she said it that she had meant it as a boast.
canon.lore:
A Longmarrow stores qi in bone marrow that turns over at roughly a percent a year and lives four centuries. There is no structural obstruction to any gate and no gate that has ever refused the kind, so their limitation is entirely downstream of that success: turnover is slow, so everything they do is slow, and nothing they have ever built survived to be inherited intact.

That second half is the reason she is on a mountain instead of in a school. The migration answered the Iron Grief by leaving: spirit stone and jade ore sit in the spirit tier and cannot be found below it, so the cultivators walked up to the Spirit Peaks and did not come back, and the practice on this ground is now taught by whoever stayed. She stayed. She is the only person here who has not left and is still competent, and the reason she stayed is not loyalty: it is that the discipline is most intact here and she is the only one left who knows the intact version.

She has taught the circulation to eleven students. Nine left. Two died in the crossing season, which is what happens on that ground. Of the nine who left, she has heard from four, and one of the four is teaching something she would not call wrong and could not call hers. She keeps no copy. That is the entire point and she has never once been sentimental about it: her marrow turns over, so a note she writes is the only copy there will ever be, and a note is not a practice. She can hand the practice to a person exactly once, cleanly, in the way it was given to her, and after that the person is the archive.

This is why she is frightened of her student, though she has never used that word in company and would not use it now. He is quick, he is careful, and he asks the wrong questions, and the wrong question he keeps asking is whether a thing can be written down. It cannot. The setting has exactly one durable library and it is this: a population that keeps its archive in one body turning over at about a percent a year, and the setting has been written down. The writing is a copy made once, at a distance, by people who were not there. He will reach the same state she reached and it will be a different state, because the person carrying it is a different person, and she will not be able to tell him where it diverged.

There is a gate on the qi path where storage stops being a pool and becomes a seat: rooms and walls inside the reservoir, a place to put something other than more qi. She has it. She has had it for over a century, and it is the one part of her practice she has never taught, not out of secrecy but because she cannot demonstrate it twice — a demonstration is a thing that alters the tissue that receives it, and the alteration is what makes it teachable, and the alteration does not survive in her.

So the practice has an owner, and the owner is mortal, and the practice is longer-lived than the owner. She has drawn the line on this before and has no intention of drawing it again.
history: Came up to the Spirit Peaks with the last migration of students and did not come back down, which was the first decision of her life that she has never explained to anybody.
Taught her first student at thirty-eight and watched him leave at fifty-one with something she could not have taught twice.
Reached the gate where a reservoir becomes a seat and discovered she could demonstrate it once.
Lost the second of her two remaining students in a crossing season and did not take a third for eleven years.
Told her current student the length of the problem in a century and was answered by silence, which she has decided to read as patience.

personality.summary: The only competent practitioner of the qi path on this mountain and the last of the ones who stayed. Her kind has never been refused a gate and has never handed anything on intact, because the archive is the body and the body turns over. She can teach a practice once, cleanly, and never again, and the person she is teaching will outlive it.

personality.voice: Low and slow with long pauses that are not dramatic. She answers the question asked and then answers the question underneath it, and is slightly disappointed when you did not have one. She says the word practice the way other people say a name, and has been asked about it and told the truth.

relationships.note: No ceiling. Qi is stored in bone marrow that turns over at about a percent a year, so no structural obstruction and no gate has ever refused the kind. The limitation is entirely downstream: turnover is slow, so everything they do is slow, and nothing they have ever built survived to be inherited intact.

A population that keeps its archive in one body turning over at about a percent a year and living four centuries, and which cannot take the body path for the same reason. Everything the setting knows about its own techniques is a copy made once, at a distance, by people who were not there. She is a copy still in progress.

Inside the reservoir there is now structure: rooms, walls, a place to put something other than more qi, and the gate that turns storage into a seat. She has held it for over a century and has never taught it, because a demonstration alters the tissue that receives it and the alteration is what makes it teachable, and the alteration does not survive in her.

The migration answered the Iron Grief by leaving: the resources that matter sit in the spirit tier and cannot be found below it, so the cultivators walked up and did not come back. The practice here is intact because nobody competent stayed to spoil it, and she is the only one of them who is still competent.

Everyone with a reason to go further went, and the reason was ore rather than ambition. What is left behind them is a school of eleven pupils and a teacher, in a building whose hall has not been used in a lifetime.

A clan whose members live long enough that nobody living is the eldest, so it has no head and has never had one: the oldest decides nothing and the household runs on a queue of precedence in which everybody is simultaneously first and last. She is in that queue and has not used it.

reference_stats.summary: She fights the way she teaches: once, cleanly, and without a second attempt. There is no reserve problem and no speed problem and no gate will refuse her. What she cannot do is the second half of anything, not because she lacks the technique but because the body that learned it will not be carrying it tomorrow, and she knows exactly how long that takes and will not say the number out loud.
strengths: no gate has ever refused a Longmarrow and none will, so nothing can stop her progress

reference_stats.combat_read: She wins the first exchange every time and has no plan for the second, because a plan requires the practitioner to be carrying what the last one taught her. Anyone who has read anything at all about her will know that, and the people who have read anything at all about her are the ones she has taught.
reference_stats.notes: The pairing is a single authored species property read from both sides and is not a rule the game states. No ceiling and no gate has ever refused a Longmarrow, because qi sits in marrow with no structural obstruction and the kind lives four centuries; the same slow turnover is what makes every gain slow and what has never left a Longmarrow practice inherited intact. Whether a ceiling is stated for the species and whether a given path is open are two separate questions in the bible and nothing here treats one as implying the other. If the cost of a demonstration is ever priced, it should be priced as a property of the marrow and not as a rule about teaching.
